newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end slightly up on industrial buying.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end slightly up on industrial buying.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange rose gently Monday as investors bought industrial companies, who will soon be able to restructure their debt with the government, brokers said.
They added, however, the market could see a technical correction Tuesday because prices were generally considered high.
Monday, the General Index rose 0.20 percent to 1,608.4 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index gained 0.49 percent to 2,148.6 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 2,174 operations, 41 stocks rose, 29 fell and 40 were stable in healthy volume of 46.6 million ($18.6 million).
Last week, the government decreed a law that will allow some companies to restructure their debt service payments involving lower interest rates and longer maturities.
"The industrials had low prices and the possibility of restructuring their debt with the state gives them better opportunities for the future," said Pablo Navarra at local brokerage Fortuna.
D'Onofrio rose 3.73 percent to 1.39 soles on 778,000 shares because officials of Switzerland's Nestle have said they are close to buying the chocolate maker.
Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- rose 0.51 percent to 5.97 soles on 504,000 shares.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru rose 0.35 percent to 5.67 soles, accounting for 47 percent of the day's volume.
